grh_bce90b883e745ab02c4f.title: The Substitute
paragraphs: Dr. Christian's overwork brings efficient nurse Agnes Spinney into the office as a temporary substitute for Judy. Spinney quickly reorganizes the office, changes long-standing suppliers, answers correspondence and assumes so many of Judy's duties that Judy feels she is being pushed aside. At the same time Judy is spending conspicuous hours with Lieutenant Tommy Bolton and helping shop for a wedding dress. Christian assumes Judy and Tommy are in love and decides that keeping Spinney will free Judy to marry and have a life of her own. Judy takes that decision as proof she has been replaced and walks out. At a community gathering Christian discovers that Tommy's real sweetheart is a blonde named Kay. Judy's secret errands with Tommy were actually helping him create a bust of Dr. Christian as the first memorial in Rivers End's new Hall of Humanity. Once the misunderstanding is cleared up, Judy returns to the office and Christian happily keeps his longtime partner beside him.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on November 1, 1944. It is listed as episode 310 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Other credited names include Leila Swift as writer and Bob Anderson as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_bcbe3d95f95522cbad7d.title: Eileen
paragraphs: Irish patriot Captain Barry O'Day hides in plain sight as a groom named Sean while British authorities search for him after an uprising. His disguise brings him close to Eileen, and the two fall in love even as Barry prepares to return to the rebel cause. When the authorities finally close in, Barry and his supporters expect a fight. grh_bc82f55338813f6876e7.title: George Washington Jenks
paragraphs: Twelve-year-old George Washington Jenks is mocked by classmates for his name, glasses and refusal to fight, but the boys do not know that rheumatic fever left him with a serious heart condition that forbids strenuous activity. When they stage another humiliating prank, George finally fights back, collapses from the strain and nearly dies. Dr. Christian explains to the ashamed boys that George has been fighting all his life against physical handicaps and that enduring them without complaint has taken more courage than any schoolyard brawl. George recovers to find his classmates waiting to welcome him back and asking him to manage their team, turning the name they once ridiculed into one they respect.

The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_bc180f72619aad91be87.title: Honeymoon
paragraphs: In Sicily, Harry reconnects with ex-gangster Plucky Mariello and meets photographer Kathy, who is determined to make her career with pictures of notorious bandit Thomasino. Her cameras become dangerous evidence as criminals, police and Harry maneuver around one another. At a railway station, police set an ambush for Thomasino while Kathy positions herself for photographs of the killing. The bandit dies in the gunfire, but Harry ends up with the camera containing the valuable images. Instead of selling the pictures back or exploiting them, he throws the camera onto a passing train, destroying Kathy's scoop and spoiling one of the few decent acts he has ever committed.
